surface.basis: Steffen et al. (2014) made a closed surface of the Homunculus from VLT/X-shooter H2 spectra that map the whole nebula: one continuous surface for each lobe, with its polar holes, trenches and protrusions. NASA publishes that model as a file for printing (17101 triangles), its z axis the nebula's pole. Smith (2006) gives the pole: an inclination of 41 degrees, the tilt of the polar axis out of the line of sight, along position angle 310 degrees; the south-east lobe approaches. The file gives neither its unit on the sky, its turn about the pole, the star's place in it, nor which end recedes: measured here on this picture (packages/bake/authoring/homunculus-nebula/model-fit.mts), the +z end recedes, the file is turned 328 degrees about the pole, a unit is 2.72 arcsec and the star is at (0.96, 0, -0.08); the model's outline then shares 86.8% with the picture's lit pixels. The patches follow the surface within 0.1 arcsec, a presentation value.
